correctness.frozen_scope_defect: The finding says general position, but its assumptions specify distinctness without excluding extra Pascal lines at a named point, and the frozen geometry verifier checked only the specified triples and distinctness, not the absence of extra flags. If distinctness is read as sufficient, this scope is false: with parameters (0,65,195,585,1755,9), all 60 lines and 80 named points are distinct, but Steiner point [731:43875:9240075] on ABCFED, ABEDCF and ADCBEF is also on ACFEBD, and the actual graph has 243 edges. The expressly generic interpretation survives. correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, Props. 3.2–3.3 of arXiv:1209.4795 establish the two labelled concurrence patterns. I generated their full relabelling orbits, built all 60 lines using the chord formula (tu,−t−u,1), and recovered all actual marked flags by exact projective intersections. At (0,1,3,9,27,81) there are 80 distinct marked points each on exactly its prescribed three lines; the absence of other marked flags is a finite list of open conditions, so the graph is constant on a nonempty Zariski open set. The independent adjacency gave a connected 8-regular graph with 240 edges, the stated exact characteristic polynomial and tree count 2^71·3^13·5^8·11^16. An integer Smith calculation on its cofactor gave 1(36), 2(7), 22, 88, 176, 528(5), 2640(4), 5280(4), with parenthesized multiplicities. The replacement geometry verifier also passes its full flag tests.
